_comment:
Which executed conformance case pins each decision. Enforced by conformance/check_decision_coverage.py.

A decision recorded only in prose is a decision nothing verifies. This audit produced two false statements of exactly that kind -- D-96 claimed its union was 'unobservable' in two SDKs (it was a fail-open approval bypass in both, corrected as D-125), and the v1.10.0 row claimed all three SDKs accept a version hint (apcore-rust has no such parameter, corrected as D-126). Neither could be caught by a test, because the sentence itself said the test was unnecessary.

UNLINKED MEANS UNCOVERED, deliberately. A case that pins a decision without saying so can be weakened by someone who does not know what it is for -- which is how approval_gate.json came to set both governance sources from one boolean and passed in all three SDKs while one of them had a bypass. If a case pins a decision, name it here.

`discriminates` is not documentation. It must say what makes the case fail when an SDK regresses; if it cannot be written, the case is not discriminating and the decision is still unpinned.

kinds: behavioural = needs a discriminating case | deferred = spec text only, no implementation to pin yet | unconstrained = the decision deliberately leaves the shape language-defined.

D-75.title: `Executor.call` must enforce the module-ID length bound at entry

D-77.title: `Registry.describe` returns a string; a structured override falls through

D-79.title: a stalled topological sort is not a cycle

D-80.title: the registry event set is closed, and `file_changed` is in it

D-84.title: a non-positive call-chain limit raises a typed error
D-84.discriminates: Both pin the WIRE code GENERAL_INVALID_INPUT, not an exception class name — a class name is shared across SDKs emitting three different codes.

D-85.title: malformed version constraints must be reportable

D-87.title: the ACL audit-block surface is a language idiom
D-87.note: The decision IS that the audit-block surface is a language idiom and deliberately unconstrained. There is no cross-SDK behaviour to pin.

D-88.title: index-keyed warning dedupe must be cleared on index shift

D-90.title: `reset()` must not substitute the cancellation handle

D-91.title: a removal method a host cannot call does not satisfy the contract

D-92.title: `TaskStoreError` must exist before it can be raised

D-93.title: the contextual-audit redaction list is a superset, and bare substrings are the point of it
D-93.discriminates: Carries signing_key / auth_header / session_id / API-Key, which only a BARE-substring matcher catches, plus a `tenant` control that must NOT be redacted.

D-94.title: symlink confinement runs before the dir/file split

D-95.title: a configuration dot-path addresses data, never the host object graph
D-95.binds_note: The defect is a JavaScript prototype-chain property; apcore-python and apcore-rust have no equivalent object graph to pollute.

D-96.title: the gate fires on the UNION of its governance sources
D-96.discriminates: The two governance sources are separate fixture fields and each case sets exactly one of them, so a gate reading either source alone turns one case red. The third is the control that stops a hardcoded `true` passing.

D-97.title: binding declarations must survive registration
D-97.discriminates: Its annotation block declares all eleven keys, so any accessor the module type fails to expose is visible as a dropped declaration at registration.

D-98.title: `$ref` sibling keys are preserved
D-98.binds_note: apcore-python and apcore-typescript already preserved sibling keys; only apcore-rust dropped them.

D-99.title: global_deadline is epoch seconds, not a monotonic reading

D-100.title: global_deadline travels in the field, not a `data` key

D-101.title: global_deadline belongs to the call tree, not the Context

D-102.title: global_deadline is recomputed unconditionally on a deserialized Context

D-104.title: the base document for a local `#/…` reference

D-105.title: the executor's ACL step MUST take the async path

D-106.title: a p99 beyond the largest bucket is that bucket, not zero

D-107.title: per-class markers are the only multi-class opt-in
D-107.discriminates: The opt-in is a PER-CLASS `multi_class` marker. `disabled_by_default` leaves it unset on both classes and expects one ID; an implementation gating on a file-level toggle cannot tell the two cases apart.

D-124.title: the node fallback is scoped to its own document

D-126.title: the v1.10.0 row is wrong about `version`
D-126.note: Three conformant answers exist by design — compile-time refusal (apcore-rust), a deprecation warning (apcore-typescript), real resolution (apcore-python). A single fixture case cannot express 'not silent' across all three; each SDK pins its own.
